project.name: masterminds-workshop
project.description: Masterminds Workshop Site is a Next.js application for event discovery and registration, workshop learning, and giveaway resource distribution, with shared content catalogs, payment integration, and email delivery.

layers.name: API Routes
layers.description: Next.js endpoint handling email-list unsubscribe token verification and suppression recording in the represented graph.

layers.name: Pages
layers.description: Event listings, workshop details, attendee setup and bonus guides provide the main workshop content and navigation.

layers.name: Giveaway Tools
layers.description: Giveaway pages, SEO layouts, resource packs and reusable prompts present AI tools, quizzes and product guides.

layers.name: Shared Libraries
layers.description: Shared event and giveaway catalogs, pricing helpers, email builders and sitemap generation support workshop and resource discovery.

layers.name: Assets
layers.description: Downloadable LinkedIn Kit and Salesman ZIP archives and their checksums provide distributable giveaway resources.

layers.name: Tests
layers.description: Catalog and LinkedIn Kit tests verify giveaway metadata, resource content, source handling and email helpers.

layers.name: Configuration
layers.description: Next.js build tracing, bundle exclusions, legacy redirects and host-specific rewrites configure delivery of workshop and giveaway routes.

tour.title: Workshop Site Overview
tour.description: Start at the events index to see how the Masterminds site presents live workshops through cards, dates, prices and links to individual events. This is the overview entry for a partial graph centered on event content, giveaways and their supporting files. Follow its catalog dependency next to learn where that presentation gets its shared event definitions.

tour.title: The Shared Event Catalog
tour.description: The event catalog supplies the listing from Step 1 with typed definitions for workshops, dinners and other gatherings. It brings together hosts, sections, SEO, registration limits, pricing, promotions, donations and attendee setup information; helpers look up events, sort upcoming live events and calculate displayed prices. Optional hero video sources, posters and mobile variants let an event choose richer media without changing the catalog structure.
tour.languageLesson: Optional TypeScript properties let event records share one model while supplying media or setup details only when those fields apply.

tour.title: From Slugs to Setup
tour.description: Building on the shared catalog, the dynamic event page resolves a slug, prepares metadata and promotion information, and passes event data to its presentation component with Stripe integration. The nested setup route presents the instructions and next steps for attendees after purchase. Read these routes as the represented navigation and content boundary; the checkout and database implementation files are outside this tour.
tour.languageLesson: In the Next.js App Router, a [slug] directory captures a route segment, while a nested setup/page.tsx creates a related URL beneath that event.

tour.title: Catalogs for Free Resources
tour.description: Alongside paid and live events, the site maintains a free AI tool catalog and a registry of giveaway pages. The former defines tool slugs, lookups and source validation, while the latter provides shared giveaway metadata. These modules establish the common vocabulary for the resource pages and checks in the following steps.

tour.title: Content Driven Giveaway Guides
tour.description: With the resource catalogs in mind, inspect Chat to Flowchart as a page, content pack and metadata layout working together. The pack holds instructions, promises, limitations and troubleshooting, while the page adds structured search data and renders the guide. The CLAUDE.md pack and layout show the same separation applied to a different setup resource.

tour.title: Prompts and Downloadable Kits
tour.description: The LinkedIn Kit extends the guide pattern from Step 5 with reusable prompt text and a downloadable archive. Its page and pack describe the resource and expose the ZIP path, while the checksum file supplies a value that can be used to verify the archive. This stop connects the content model to the concrete files a visitor can download.

tour.title: Creative Tool Resource Pages
tour.description: The film resource applies the same page, pack and prompt organization to an animated video guide with gallery and repository links. Its layout supplies search metadata separately from the guide content. Compare the Concat page to see another resource page using shared free AI tool presentation utilities, whose implementations are outside the represented files.

tour.title: Quizzes and Bonus Learning
tour.description: The quiz pages reuse the guide pattern to explain two distinct assessments: behavioral intensity from B0 to B10 and capability levels on a 0–40 scale. Their packs hold explanatory content and links, while the quizzes themselves run on an external site. The automatic lead magnet guide demonstrates a longer learning resource with an embedded prompt, instructions and a sample PDF link.

tour.title: Email Content and Preferences
tour.description: After seeing the resources visitors receive, inspect the shared helpers that validate giveaway links and names and construct generic or keyword-specific email content. The unsubscribe route represents the corresponding preference boundary: its GET and POST handlers verify tokens and record suppressions for email list management. These files explain content preparation and unsubscribe behavior without establishing a complete delivery pipeline.

tour.title: Catalog Based Search Discovery
tour.description: The sitemap connects the resource catalog from Step 4 to search discovery by importing the shared free AI tool slug catalog. It combines tool page URLs with home, giveaway and lead magnet entries, assigning modification times, update frequencies and priorities. This makes the catalog an input to both resource lookup and the generated list of discoverable URLs.

tour.title: Build Assets and Routing
tour.description: Next.js configuration determines how the pages and resources from earlier steps are packaged and reached. Its tracing rules include private prompt pack assets for the relevant API handlers and exclude non-image event media, including video, from server bundles, while fixing the Turbopack root to this project. Legacy and portal redirects plus host-specific root rewrites direct requests to the intended destinations.

tour.title: Checks Across Resource Boundaries
tour.description: Finish by reading the tests that protect the shared resource contracts introduced throughout the tour. The free AI tool tests check catalog lookup, source handling and formatting, while the LinkedIn Kit tests connect registered giveaway content with its pack, prompt and email helpers. These represented tests show which resource assumptions are checked; they do not establish coverage of the unrepresented checkout or database flows.
